result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.cmty_louvain_levels()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Return the community partition at each level of the Louvain algorithm. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L26296-L26349){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.cmty_louvain_levels( resolution=1.0, seed=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Louvain community levels](/assets/graphs/cmty-louvain-levels.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="A two-by-four ladder, A to D on top and E to H below. Left, Louvain's first level (seed 0) pairs neighbors along the rails into four communities, A, B in the accent color, C, D in teal, E, F in violet and G, H in gold. Right, the next level merges those pairs into two communities, the left half A, B, E, F (accent) and the right half C, D, G, H (teal)." width="100%"} Louvain builds communities bottom-up: it first groups nodes into small communities, then collapses each community into a single node and repeats on the smaller graph. Each round gives a coarser partition, so the levels form a hierarchy, from many small groups to a few large ones. `cmty_louvain()` keeps only the last level; this method returns all of them, to explore communities at several scales (neighborhoods within districts, teams within departments). The graph must be undirected. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [resolution]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1.0]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Resolution parameter (default 1); larger values favor smaller communities. [seed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Random seed for the node visiting order. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[dict[int, int]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : One node-to-community dictionary per level, finest first. Labels are numbered in order of the lowest node ID in each community. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is directed. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Each level is one round of local moving (the fast queue-based variant) followed by aggregation; a level is recorded whenever the partition is coarser than the previous one, and the run stops when no node moves. The last level, with the same seed, is the partition `cmty_louvain()` would find. Mirrors NetworkX's `louvain_partitions` (which yields lists of node sets). ## Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#f166e4a9 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec g = ec.Graph().add_smallworld_graph(n=60, k=4, p=0.05, seed=1) levels = g.cmty_louvain_levels(seed=2) [len(set(level.values())) for level in levels] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` [15, 7] ``` ::: :::
